cases.description: When validation is turned on and the JSON instance conforms to the schema (a simple object with a required string property), walk should return a successful ValidationResult.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.failure() containing a message about missing required property 'name'
cases.description: When validation is on but the instance is missing a required property, walk must collect a validation error.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.success() – no validation messages (validation is skipped)
cases.description: When the `validate` flag is false, walk must not perform any schema validation, even if the instance is invalid.
The method should fail fast when a null ExecutionContext is supplied.
The method should fail fast when a null JsonNode is supplied.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.success() – array conforms to schema (type array, items integer)
cases.description: Walk must correctly handle an array node and validate each element against the schema.
When the instance is a primitive value that does not match the expected type, walk should report a type‑validation error.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.success() – recursion resolved without stack overflow
cases.description: Schema defines a `$recursiveAnchor` and the instance contains a self‑reference; walk must follow the anchor and finish successfully.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.success() – schema recognized as resource root, no extra resolution performed
cases.description: When `isSchemaResourceRoot()` returns true, walk should treat the schema as a top‑level resource and avoid unnecessary ancestor look‑ups.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.failure() – contains a single message about missing required property 'name' and stops after first error because failFast is true
cases.description: When the ExecutionContext is configured with failFast, walk should abort after the first validation error instead of collecting all possible errors.

cases.expected: ValidationResult.success() – includes annotation messages (e.g., "default applied") if schema defines defaults
cases.description: When the ExecutionContext is set to collect annotations, walk should still succeed but the resulting ValidationResult must contain annotation messages generated by the validator.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException – malformed URI in $ref causes parsing failure
cases.description: When the instance contains a `$ref` with an invalid URI, the walk method should throw an IllegalArgumentException while trying to resolve the reference.

cases.expected: IllegalArgumentException – MissingNode cannot be processed as a regular JSON value
cases.description: Passing a `MissingNode` (Jackson's representation of a non‑existent node) should cause the walk method to reject the input with an IllegalArgumentException.

cases.expected: IllegalStateException – schema validators have not been initialized before walking
cases.description: If a `JsonSchema` instance is created but `initializeValidators()` is never called, invoking `walk` should fail with an IllegalStateException because the internal validator list is null.

cases.expected: StackOverflowError – infinite recursion when resolving a circular $ref without a $recursiveAnchor
cases.description: A schema that references itself via `$ref` but does not declare `$recursiveAnchor` should cause the walk method to recurse indefinitely, eventually throwing a StackOverflowError.
